body:
Test suites create `mkdtempSync` fixture directories under `tmpdir()` and never remove most of them. A sweep of one developer machine found 63,656 /tmp entries / 843 MB, of which 54,065 were stale fixture dirs older than 24h; during an active test run the rate is ~1,000 new dirs/hour. This repo already hit a /tmp inode-exhaustion incident from leaked fixtures (2026-09-03 issue-lanes batch), which surfaces as unrelated, confusing failures mid-run. GitHub issue: #1043. Near neighbour (do not merge the two): #1042, hung adlc-hook processes — its hangs skip the `finally` cleanup in hook tests that are otherwise correct, so it causes a SLICE of this symptom, but this ticket's volume comes from files that leak on a clean exit.

Two failure shapes, both verified:
1. NO cleanup at all — 25 files call mkdtempSync and never call rmSync/rimraf. Example: packages/prosecute/test/helpers.mjs:14,25 mints a fixture per call and nothing removes it (754 leaked `adlc-prosecute-` dirs observed).
2. PARTIAL cleanup — packages/tickets/test/generation-descriptor.test.mjs calls mkdtempSync at lines 35, 240, 453, 460 but rmSync only twice; the last two leak (1,152 dirs observed).

390 files call mkdtempSync, so the defence must be mechanical, not a hand audit.

DECISIONS ALREADY TAKEN (do not relitigate; human-approved at P0):
- Enforcement is a RATCHET: the guard fails closed for any new or modified test file, and carries an explicit allowlist of today's non-compliant files that may only ever SHRINK. Do not attempt a 390-file conversion in this ticket.
- NO new shared helper module. Each file keeps its own small `after()` + rmSync registry — the pattern PR #1014 used in plugins/adlc-cursor/test/mcp-wrapper.test.mjs (14 leaked dirs per run -> 0). The guard enforces the STRUCTURE, not a specific import. Rationale: no cross-package test-helper precedent exists in this repo today, and a shared module would either put test-only code in a published package or create deep relative imports.
- RAILS ARE EMPTY ON PURPOSE, and this is a correction to the original P0 intent (the human approved "freeze the guard"): a rail on scripts/test/tmp-fixture-boundary.test.mjs would be self-defeating, because the in-session PreToolUse hook denies Write to any declared rail — the lane could never CREATE the file. Freezing it is a FOLLOW-UP ticket once the file exists on main. Do not add rails to this ticket and do not set ADLC_RAILS_BYPASS to work around one.
- Production (non-test) mkdtempSync is OUT OF SCOPE and must not be flagged: 12+ files use it legitimately for atomic writes, clones and locks (packages/tickets/lib/edit.mjs, packages/autopilot/lib/lock.mjs, packages/gate-fuzzing/lib/clone.mjs, ...). The guard scans test files only.

Build it in the style of the existing deterministic scan, scripts/test/ticket-store-boundary.test.mjs: detector logic exported from the test file itself, an APPROVED set for sanctioned exceptions, and a test that plants a violation to prove the detector bites. Wire it into the `scripts` CI segment (scripts/run-tests.mjs already runs `node --test scripts/test/*.test.mjs`).

WHAT "REGISTERS CLEANUP" MEANS (the detector contract — file-level presence of rmSync is NOT enough; packages/tickets/test/generation-descriptor.test.mjs contains rmSync and still leaks two of its four fixtures):
Pair every mkdtempSync call with a removal of THAT binding. A call site is compliant when its result is bound to a name (const X = mkdtempSync(...)) and that same name X appears in the same file as any of:
  (a) rmSync(X ...            — direct removal;
  (b) cleanup(X) / a local one-argument helper whose body itself calls rmSync on its parameter;
  (c) registration into a tracked collection that is drained in an after( ... ) hook, e.g. dirs.add(X) / dirs.push(X) where the hook rmSyncs each member.
An UNASSIGNED mkdtempSync call (result passed inline, never bound) is non-compliant by definition: nothing can remove it.
The detector is a regex/AST scan over test files only; it never executes them.

Acceptance criteria:
1. A deterministic guard flags a test file that calls mkdtempSync without registering cleanup, and passes a file that registers it. Verify: node --test scripts/test/tmp-fixture-boundary.test.mjs
2. The guard bites on a PLANTED violation (a fixture-creating test file with no cleanup is detected), proving it is not vacuous. Verify: node --test scripts/test/tmp-fixture-boundary.test.mjs
3. The allowlist is shrink-only: the suite fails if an allowlisted file has become compliant and was left in the list, so the ratchet cannot silently stall. Verify: node --test scripts/test/tmp-fixture-boundary.test.mjs
4. Production (non-test) mkdtempSync call sites are not flagged. Verify: node --test scripts/test/tmp-fixture-boundary.test.mjs
5. These converted offenders are removed from the allowlist and leak nothing: packages/prosecute/test/helpers.mjs, packages/tickets/test/generation-descriptor.test.mjs, plugins/adlc-cursor/test/scaffold.test.mjs, packages/runner/test/p0-p1-gates.test.mjs, packages/prosecute/test/record-unknown-ticket-refusal.test.mjs. Verify: node --test scripts/test/tmp-fixture-boundary.test.mjs && node --test packages/prosecute/test/*.test.mjs && node --test packages/tickets/test/generation-descriptor.test.mjs && node --test plugins/adlc-cursor/test/scaffold.test.mjs && node --test packages/runner/test/p0-p1-gates.test.mjs
6. MEASURED end to end and immune to concurrent activity: running the converted suites under a PRIVATE empty TMPDIR leaves that dir empty. Do NOT count entries in the shared /tmp — another session on the same machine creates ~1,000 dirs/hour, so a shared-/tmp before/after count both false-fails and false-passes. Verify: d=$(mktemp -d); TMPDIR="$d" node --test packages/prosecute/test/*.test.mjs packages/tickets/test/generation-descriptor.test.mjs plugins/adlc-cursor/test/scaffold.test.mjs packages/runner/test/p0-p1-gates.test.mjs >/dev/null 2>&1; left=$(find "$d" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 | wc -l); rm -rf "$d"; test "$left" -eq 0
7. The whole suite still passes. Verify: npm test
title: Stop test fixtures leaking mkdtemp dirs, and guard the pattern deterministically (#1043)
